questions.question: The two questions that route any transaction to its journal are:
options: Did money move, and in which direction — or if not, what happened?
Is it big, and is it monthly?
Cash or card, and who authorised it?
Debit or credit, and which ledger?

questions.question: R2 000 received from a debtor is entered in:
options: The DJ, because it relates to a credit sale
The CRJ's Debtors Control column, plus the debtor's page — never Sales

questions.question: Why does paying a creditor never touch Trading Stock?
options: The payment settles the debt; the stock was recorded the day it arrived via the CJ
Creditors are not linked to stock

questions.question: A debt written off enters the:
options: General Journal — no money moved, no goods moved

questions.question: The credit sale to L. Dube (R3 000, mark-up 25% on cost) writes in the DJ:
options: Sales R3 000 and Cost of Sales R2 400
Sales R3 000 and Cost of Sales R2 250

questions.question: Across the month, L. Dube appears in THREE journals because:
options: She sold goods to the business
One customer can generate a sale (DJ), a return (DAJ) and a receipt (CRJ) — her page gathers all three

questions.question: The return of damaged stock to Metro (R800) is recorded in the:
options: CAJ, with Metro's page debited and a debit note issued

subtopics.title: Posting the Month and Proving It

questions.question: Bank's closing balance from the month (in 28 000, out 11 000) is:
Debtors Control closes at R500 debit, which must equal:
options: The list of debtors — Dube R500, Naidoo closed

questions.question: The month's trial balance levels at:
The receipt from Dube, in equation terms, was:
options: A swap inside A — Bank up, Debtors down

subtopics.title: The Control Web Around the Month

questions.question: Under the perpetual system, the R2 400 Trading Stock balance is described as a 'claim' because:
options: The stocktake can test it — a shortfall now has a name and a size
It belongs to the owner personally

questions.question: Naidoo's write-off was ethically sound because:
options: It followed documented follow-up and was recorded with a narration — prudence on evidence, accountability in ink

questions.question: Metro's invoice earned recording only after:
options: The three-document match: order, delivery note, invoice telling one story

questions.question: Dube's R2 000 payment goes through the money-in door but is NOT a sale because:
options: Her sale went through the trust-out door weeks ago; this paper only settles her page

questions.question: The paper that slides through the odd-jobs door is:
options: Naidoo's dead debt — no money, no goods, one explaining sentence

questions.question: The sorting reflex is fast because:
options: It is two questions asked per paper, not eleven procedures memorised

questions.question: Dube's page at month end reads:
The stock drawer's R2 400 means:
options: Goods costing R2 400 should be standing on the shelf, checkable by counting

questions.question: The level weigh-in at R32 500 certifies that:
options: Eleven events crossed six doors and two ledgers with no rand lost or invented
The bank agrees with the till

questions.question: Stop two of the Friday walk checks:
options: A sample of shelf items counted against the stock drawer's claim

questions.question: 'Had Naidoo's R300 been chased in week one' teaches that:
options: Debts age badly — the debtors list must be walked weekly, not discovered at write-off

questions.question: The walk is possible at all because:
options: The books give every question a record to check against
The owner has a good memory
